properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 1 at 2:06AM CDT by NWS Little Rock AR
properties.description:
At 205 AM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Jacksonville, moving southeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
North Little Rock...              Sherwood...
Jacksonville...                   Lonoke...
Little Rock AFB...                Sisemore...
Meto...                           McAlmont...
South Bend...                     Protho Junction...
Gravel Ridge...                   Bevis Corner...
Furlow...                         Kerr...
Pettus...                         Galloway...
Fairview in Lonoke County...
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued August 1 at 1:50AM CDT until August 1 at 4:45AM CDT by NWS Paducah KY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Caldwell County in western Kentucky...
Lyon County in western Kentucky...

* WHEN...Until 445 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 150 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Princeton, Eddyville, Cravens Bay Campground, Demumbers Bay
Campground, Birmingham Ferry Recreation Area, Hillman Ferry
Campground, Land Between The Lakes Area, Farmersville, Creswell,
Cobb, Kuttawa, Fredonia and Fryer.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 1 at 1:46AM CDT by NWS Paducah KY
properties.description:
At 146 AM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Farmersville, or near Princeton, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Princeton, Eddyville, Creswell, Olney, Farmersville, and Fryer.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 24 in Kentucky between Mile Markers 53 and 56.
Interstate 69 in Kentucky between Mile Markers 70 and 87.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued July 31 at 9:52PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden, Three Rivers...Major
flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 39.2 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 39.0
feet on 10/21/2013.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued July 31 at 9:29PM CDT until August 1 at 5:00AM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in St Louis has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Missouri...

Meramec River near Steelville.

River forecasts are based on observed precipitation and forecast
precipitation for the next 24 hours.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast due to heavy rain.

* WHERE...Meramec River near Steelville.

* WHEN...From this evening to late tonight.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:15 PM CDT Friday the stage was 10.2 feet.
- Forecast...No forecast is available for this location.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Rainfall heavier than forecast could cause river levels to rise even
higher than predicted. The National Weather Service will monitor this
developing situation and issue follow up statements as conditions
change.

This product, along with additional weather and stream information,
is available at https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/lsx

properties.title: Flood Watch issued July 31 at 9:04PM CDT until August 3 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Quad Cities IA IL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Quad Cities has issued a Flood
Watch for the following rivers in Iowa...

Wapsipinicon River near De Witt 4S affecting Scott and Clinton
Counties.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/quadcities.

The next statement will be issued by Saturday evening.

* WHAT...Flooding is possible.

* WHERE...Wapsipinicon River near De Witt 4S.

* WHEN...From Sunday morning to Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 11.0 feet...Water affects County Road E63 north of the
river near Toronto and affects the lowest roads in Buena Vista.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM CDT Friday the stage was 7.3 feet.
- Forecast...Flood stage may be reached Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Air Quality Alert issued July 31 at 9:32AM PDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
AQAMSO

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory due to smoke from wildfires.

Air Quality Index ranging from Moderate to Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.

* WHERE...All Areas on the Nez Perce Reservation.

* WHEN...Until 10:00 AM PDT Monday August 3.

* IMPACTS...Those who experience health effects from smoke include
children under 18, elders, pregnant women, people with asthma
or have difficulty breathing, diabetes, heart problems or
otherwise compromised health, and people who have high exposure
(those who work, exercise, or spend extensive time outdoors).
properties.instruction:
Under the most severe pollution level, sensitive groups should avoid
outdoor exposure and limit indoor activities, and everyone should
restrict their outdoor activities.

Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
https://healthandwelfare.idaho.gov/health-wellness/environmental-
health/wildfire-smoke
Idaho Smoke Information Hotline: 1-800-345-1007
